feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 10 (mass 0.45 kg, body_length 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.10 m) is the best so far at 785.3, with the oval 20/20 at 1.97 s, the s-bend 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.277, and the slalom 6/20 with progress 0.76 and line_loss_events 1.10. Iteration 9 (mass 0.5 kg) reached 741.9, so each yaw-inertia reduction has helped the slalom. Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.09 m) showed that more turn authority raises s-bend jitter to 0.342 and cuts slalom progress, so do not narrow the track. Body_length 0.11 m continues the yaw-inertia lever with about 8 percent less inertia, which is a smaller step than the mass steps, to limit overshoot risk. Next-race rules: if slalom progress rises above 0.76 and s-bend steering_oscillation stays under 0.35 with the s-bend at 19/20 or better, keep body_length 0.11 m as the new best geometry. If slalom progress rises but line_loss_events stay at about 1.1 or more, keep the geometry fixed and report the heading and speed at first line loss, since the controller entry speed is the next lever. If s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35 or the oval loses any trial, return body_length to 0.12 m.
requested_changes: If s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, the oval loses any trial, or the score falls below 785.3, return body_length to 0.12 m with mass 0.45 kg (iteration 10, measured 0.277 on the s-bend and 20/20 on the oval).

If slalom progress rises above 0.76 and finishes rise above 6/20 with the s-bend holding, keep body_length 0.11 m and test mass 0.42 kg with body_length 0.11 m, since mass 0.5 to 0.45 kg (iterations 9 to 10) raised finishes from 2/20 to 6/20. Keep the mass at or above the 0.4 kg lower bound.

If slalom line_loss_events stay at about 1.1 or more with progress above 0.76, do not reduce yaw inertia further. Keep wheel_track at 0.10 m (iteration 8 showed narrowing adds jitter) and report the heading and speed at first line loss so the controller entry speed can be the next lever.
